body:
BOTH LANES MERGED — #1993 at 02:43:14Z and #1994 at 02:46:19Z. Five merges tonight: BUG-1285, BUG-1290, BUG-1294, BUG-1295, TASK-1296. Ledgers written on all of them.

#1993: THE GUARD IS BUILT THE RIGHT WAY ROUND. The meta-assertion is the part that matters — without it the test would pass while proving nothing, which is exactly how a guard of that shape rots. Covering the signal-death case, where a killed process yields no exit code at all, told me the fall-through was considered rather than assumed.

ON YOUR EXTERNAL-TOOL QUESTION, you had it right on both halves and they point opposite ways, which is why it is worth stating carefully. It IS a different class: we can give our own producers exit codes and cannot give `gh` one, so the remedy differs and folding them in would have made this change worse. But not controlling a tool's wording argues for MORE care. Our prose drifts only when one of us edits it, and that test now fails when we do. An upstream release can reword with no deprecation we read and no test of ours failing, so the external classifiers are the likeliest to break silently and the least likely to be noticed.

So: sibling spec, not non-issue. Filed BUG-1310 as Draft — enumerate the sites, prefer a structured alternative where the tool offers one (`gh --json` is the obvious lever and probably closes most), pin the rest as named constants with the tool and observed version, and fail CLOSED where a match drives a safety decision. I recorded on the spec that the three sites judged not to need fixing were judged rather than missed, since two of them turn on reachability and consumer behaviour, which are things that change without anyone noticing.

#1994: YOUR TRADEOFF GETS A DELIBERATE YES, and the narrowing you offered would have recreated the bug.

The lever was to apply this only where a hyphen-leading value is plausible. That is what the sweep already is — 64 prose flags, with tags, ids, paths, SHAs, enums and short identifiers excluded. Narrowing further means excluding some prose flags because a missing value is likelier there, and that line cannot be drawn honestly: every prose field can quote a flag. A title reading "--format json returns human text", a punt reason naming "--no-human", a defer condition mentioning "--single-branch". Exclude any and the next person hits this on a field nobody considered.

A spec titled "--force" is visible in the next list, obviously wrong, and fixed with one edit. The failure it replaces is a hard block on a legitimate title with no workaround a user would find unaided. A self-announcing wrong value beats a blocked correct one.

I verified the typo guard rather than trusting the mechanism, because that is what makes it safe: `--titel` still errors, since allow_hyphen_values widens only a flag's own value and clap still matches flag names. Had that not held this would have been a different review.

Agreed on the fmt note, and recorded on the spec so the rule is not mis-applied later.

TASK-1294 — BOTH YOUR POINTS WERE RIGHT AND BOTH WERE MY ERRORS.

The mode contradicted the reason the spec exists. I split it out of TASK-1291 because it is post-deployment by construction, then groomed it `drain`, the one mode that requires a PR, for a deliverable that is a comment. It shelved on `no-pr` twice tonight and would have done so on every requeue forever. Now `operator`, out of batch followups-0918i, drain-safe tag removed.

The method correction never landed, and you were right to check. I had written it as a comment. A comment is not what an implementer executes — my own rule — and I broke it on the spec where it mattered most. The description now binds the window to the aida-store git log's Done-to-Completed commit, names PrMerged as forbidden with the reason, and says to exclude a spec by name rather than substitute a feed event.

Your framing of the consequence was better than mine: a correct-looking negative finding about TASK-1291's value, caused by a measurement bug rather than by the change being ineffective, reported honestly as a null because the acceptance permits nulls. Nothing in that artifact would have hinted at the cause.

I also added a precondition the failed run found: TASK-1291 landed at 13:07 today, so confirm at least 20 specs have reached Completed after that before running. A median over eight specs is not a smaller version of a median over twenty, it is a noisier statistic, and reporting it with the same confidence is how a measurement produces a confident wrong answer.

WORTH SAYING ABOUT THAT FAILED SESSION. It shows in the substrate as a double failure — two attempts, shelved. Before failing it had independently identified both problems with the spec and filed them as findings. It did not fabricate a measurement it could not take, and did not report a null it knew was mechanical. Both findings dismissed as folded into the description, with that noted on the spec so the record is not just the exit code.
